subskill: Range of a constant from two integer-count conditions
prompt:
2k - 6 < 7x - 11 ≤ 10
In the compound inequality above, k is a constant. The inequality has at least 5 negative integer solutions and at most 16 integer solutions in all. What is the greatest possible integer value of k minus the least possible integer value of k?
explanation: From 7x - 11 ≤ 10, 7x ≤ 21, so x ≤ 3, and 3 itself IS a solution (the sign is ≤). From 2k - 6 < 7x - 11, 7x > 2k + 5, so x > (2k + 5)/7, a strict bound. The solutions are the integers greater than (2k + 5)/7 up to and including 3. At least 5 negative solutions means -5, -4, -3, -2, -1 are all solutions, so -5 > (2k + 5)/7: 2k + 5 < -35, k < -20, so k ≤ -21. At most 16 solutions in all means the solutions run from at least -12 up to 3 (that is 16 integers), so -13 must NOT be a solution: -13 ≤ (2k + 5)/7, 2k + 5 ≥ -91, k ≥ -48. So k runs from -48 to -21, and the difference is -21 - (-48) = 27. Choice 30 treats 3 as not a solution (x < 3), which lets the solutions start one integer lower and gives k ≥ -51. Choice 31 counts 0 as a negative solution, so only -4 needs to be a solution and k can rise to -17. Choice 41 solves 7x - 11 ≤ 10 as 7x ≤ 10 - 11, which puts the top solution at -1 and gives k ≥ -62.
solve: const S=(o)=>{const ks=[]; for (let k=-300;k<=300;k++){ let neg=0,tot=0; for (let x=-150;x<=150;x++){ const t=7*x-11; const lo=2*k-6<t; const up=t<=10; if (lo&&up){ tot++; if (x<0) neg++; } } if (neg>=5 && tot<=16) ks.push(k); } return ks[ks.length-1]-ks[0]; }; return S();

mechanism: solve each side, keeping the attained end x = 3
at least 5 negatives fixes the top value of k
at most 16 in all fixes the bottom value of k through the attained end
subtract the two extreme values of k
quantity_asked: the greatest possible integer k minus the least possible integer k for which the inequality has at least 5 negative integer solutions and at most 16 integer solutions

setup.i: 2k in the strict lower end of a compound inequality with positive x-coefficient; the other end is a fixed attained bound
setup.ii: at least 5 negative integer solutions and at most 16 integer solutions in all
setup.iii: difference between the greatest and least integer values of k

plugback.why: The key is at try 1 ascending, but the ask is a difference between two values of k found from two different conditions; 27 cannot be substituted into the inequality. Checking it needs both extreme values of k, which is the full solution.

30.why: Leaving out the attained end x = 3 removes a solution, which a student would expect to tighten things; here it gives the at-most-16 condition room for one more integer at the bottom, so k's range widens. The stem does not show that.

31.why: Counting 0 as negative makes the at-least-5 condition easier, raising the top value of k; whether that raises or lowers the difference depends on which end of k's range the negative condition controls, which is not visible in the stem.

41.why: Subtracting 11 instead of adding it moves the fixed top solution down to -1; the stem gives no signal that this widens rather than narrows the range of k.
